facts.text: The Central King Building was built as the Central Commercial and Manual Training School. The school was founded in 1911 and the building was dedicated on January 31, 1912.
It is a seven-story building of brick and terra cotta in the Jacobean style, with four corner towers.
The school had a forge, a foundry, a sewing room, a sheet-metal room and a wood shop, plus an auditorium seating 1,500.
The building housed Central High School until NJIT bought it in 2010.
On April 13, 2017, more than 200 students, alumni, faculty, staff and friends attended the ribbon cutting of the renovated Central King Building.
